findings.reason: a worker cannot identify the four runs to record, and cannot tell whether the set is the three upstreams or a fourth, so the recording arm would be filled arbitrarily.
findings.text: §13's done-when says "The node records, for the four runs named above, where their promotion is recorded and why the row read returned none", but no run id is named anywhere in §13 and the evidence paragraph (line 105) first says the request waited "on three such runs" and then queries "the four landed runs", so the count conflicts and the referent set does not exist

findings.reason: a worker could implement the release by reading the ledger or git and never touch the run store, passing arm 1 while failing arm 4, so one verdict cannot close both mechanisms and the node should be split or the second guarantee moved to its own section.
findings.text: §13's deliverable states two separate guarantees: the wait leaves within one admission pass "read from wherever promotions are recorded today" (repairing the stale readiness read) and "A run recorded as promoted and landed has a row in the run store for as long as its run record exists" (repairing a run-store row loss); these are distinct write paths and the done-when tests them as separate arms

findings.reason: the section's own concern is a probe re-run every few seconds, so with no interval or bound fixed the gate can be satisfied by an implementation that sets both arbitrarily wide and the next recurrence of the lock storm is not bounded.
findings.text: §14 requires the probe to run "no more often than a stated interval" and to be stopped when it "runs longer than a stated bound", but the section states neither value, and the done-when arms are phrased in terms of "the interval" and "the bound"

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the dependency plan building-a-plan-queues-all-of-it and its #s3 resolve, and both cited run records (r-20261121T201937629427-anchored-flight-key-s18, r-20261122T072450492220-work-flows-to-the-lane-s67) exist on disk; the run ids are artifacts, not hrefs, so no .html resolution applies.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §13's done-when requires recording "the four runs named above" although the section names no run id and its evidence counts three such runs (line 105) not four; §14's arms reference "the interval" and "the bound" which the section never states.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both sections put each arm's log "under the run directory", a durable path that survives the run, not a scratchpad or node-local temp.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §13 and §14 name no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags, and no changelog prose; they describe the mechanism (a wait releases when its upstream run has landed; a probe is single-flight and bounded).
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — each section's stated root cause matches its cited evidence (the readiness check reads stale per-run state files and the run store lost rows; every polling reader runs the probe concurrently), each endpoint is reachable and its measure can fail, and neither section prescribes a code path, step sequence, formula or function to extend.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §13's deliverable carries two distinct guarantees (a wait releases by reading the promotion record, and the run store retains a row per landed run), which one gate cannot close on one verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — _document's new s7 wait on s11 resolves (section 11 exists and is implementable), and the plan's own s3/s4/s8/s9/s11 targets all exist; s13 and s14 are independent additions that declare and receive no wait, which their content supports.
